technical_and_design_decisions: Target platform is an existing Spring XD-style distributed runtime; processors and sinks are delivered as deployable stream modules registered in the module registry, not as changes to the core container.

U2 (Python): adopt a process-based integration (launch CPython via ProcessBuilder, exchange data over stdin/stdout with a defined line/record marshalling format) rather than Jython, so that native libraries such as NumPy/pandas are usable; a short spike will confirm feasibility before implementation.

U3 (R): adopt a process-based integration (Rscript over stdin/stdout) as the default; rJava/Renjin evaluated in a spike and kept as a pluggable alternative binding only if the spike shows clear benefit, to keep consistency with the Python processor design.

U4 (Hive): sink writes data files to HDFS using the Hadoop HDFS client and registers/updates external Hive tables via Hive metastore/JDBC; Kerberos-secured clusters supported through JAAS/keytab configuration.

U6-U8 (security): use Spring Security for admin endpoint authentication/authorization; security definitions map REST API entities to role/group policies; ACL model supports create/destroy/view permissions on streams with default of all authenticated users; ACLs and security definitions are persisted in the existing distributed coordination store (ZooKeeper) so shell, REST API, and Admin UI share one policy source enforced server-side.

U1 is documentation-led: document existing SSL/HTTPS and Basic authentication configuration properties for admin endpoints with verified examples; minimal code changes (only configuration property fixes if gaps are found).
U5 upgrade aligns the whole dependency tree to Spring Framework 4.1.1 (milestone) via the build's dependency management; deprecated API usage is migrated rather than shimmed.
All features include reference documentation (asciidoc) and runnable samples as part of done.
assumptions: An existing Spring XD-like codebase, Gradle build, CI pipeline, and automated test infrastructure are already in place; no greenfield project setup is required.
A Hadoop/Hive test cluster (including a Kerberos-secured instance) is available for U4 integration testing.
Python (2.7/3.x) and R runtimes are installed on the hosts used for U2/U3 integration tests.

Estimates represent the hands-on development effort of a single experienced developer familiar with the codebase, and include design, implementation, unit/integration testing, and documentation, but exclude elapsed calendar time, vacations, and external dependencies' wait time.

The specification's background references to Spring Framework 6.0/Java 17 are generic context; this increment follows U5 and targets Spring Framework 4.1.1 on the existing Java baseline of the product.
Admin UI is an existing Angular-based application; U8 changes are incremental to it and require no new UI design work.
U1 requires no new security features in code beyond documenting and verifying existing configuration knobs.
External milestone dependencies (Spring 4.1.1, Hadoop/Hive, Python, R) are stable enough that integration issues can be fixed within the estimated effort.
